parameters.relayBrief: safe-refactor v1.0.0 — Reshape code without changing what it does. Write down the invariants, pin today's behaviour with tests, refactor in the open, then prove every invariant still holds.

parameters.title: Map the code
parameters.instructions:
Read the code under ${src_path} and write ${notes_dir}/refactor.md with four sections:
"## Today" (how the code is structured now and what makes it hard to change),
"## Target" (the shape it should have and why that is better),
"## Steps" (the moves that get there, each small enough to review on its own) and
"## Invariants" (the behaviour that must not change, one per line as `INV1: ...`, `INV2: ...`, at least three).
Name real files and functions, not categories.

parameters.title: Pin current behaviour
parameters.instructions:
Write characterization tests under ${test_path} that pin each invariant against the current code, and name
the invariant each test covers (for example `INV2` in the test name or a comment). They must pass now. Do not
change ${src_path}.

parameters.title: Refactor
parameters.instructions:
Restructure ${src_path} as planned in ${notes_dir}/refactor.md. Keep public behaviour identical, keep ${test_cmd}
green after each move and keep ${lint_cmd} clean.

parameters.title: Prove the invariants
parameters.instructions:
Read the plan, the pinned tests and the refactored code, then write ${notes_dir}/refactor-review.md: one line
per invariant naming its id, whether it still holds and the test that shows it, then the steps from the plan
that were done, changed or dropped, and why.

parameters.title: Refactor gate
parameters.instructions: The refactor is done only when everything still passes

nodeGroups.name: Understand and pin
nodeGroups.description:
A refactor changes the shape of code, never its behaviour. Before anything moves, you decide what must stay true
and you pin it with tests that pass against today's code. Nothing under the source paths changes in this phase.

nodeGroups.name: Reshape
nodeGroups.description:
Now move the code toward the target, following the steps in the plan. The pinned tests are the contract: change
the code until they pass, never the tests until the code passes. If an invariant turns out wrong, stop and say so
instead of rewriting its test.

work_packages.title: Map the code
work_packages.instructions:
Read the code under ${src_path} and write ${notes_dir}/refactor.md with four sections:
"## Today" (how the code is structured now and what makes it hard to change),
"## Target" (the shape it should have and why that is better),
"## Steps" (the moves that get there, each small enough to review on its own) and
"## Invariants" (the behaviour that must not change, one per line as `INV1: ...`, `INV2: ...`, at least three).
Name real files and functions, not categories.

checklist.assert: the plan has Today, Target, Steps and Invariants sections
checklist.cmd: for section in Today Target Steps Invariants; do grep -q "^## $section" ${notes_dir}/refactor.md || exit 1; done

checklist.assert: the plan lists at least three numbered invariants

checklist.judge: Is this plan grounded in the actual code — does it name real files and functions, describe a concrete target shape and list invariants a test can check? FAIL if any section is generic enough to fit any codebase, if an invariant is not observable behaviour, or if a step is too large to review on its own.

work_packages.title: Pin current behaviour
work_packages.instructions:
Write characterization tests under ${test_path} that pin each invariant against the current code, and name
the invariant each test covers (for example `INV2` in the test name or a comment). They must pass now. Do not
change ${src_path}.

checklist.assert: characterization tests were added or changed
checklist.cmd: git diff --name-only ${base_ref} -- ${test_path} | grep -q . || git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- ${test_path} | grep -q .

checklist.assert: no source file changed while pinning
the suite passes against today's code
every invariant id from the plan appears in the tests
checklist.cmd: ids=$(grep -oE '^INV[0-9]+' ${notes_dir}/refactor.md) || exit 1; for id in $ids; do grep -rqw "$id" ${test_path} || { echo "$id is not pinned"; exit 1; }; done

work_packages.title: Refactor
work_packages.instructions:
Restructure ${src_path} as planned in ${notes_dir}/refactor.md. Keep public behaviour identical, keep ${test_cmd}
green after each move and keep ${lint_cmd} clean.

checklist.cmd: git diff --name-only ${base_ref} -- ${src_path} | grep -q . || git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- ${src_path} | grep -q .

checklist.assert: the pinned tests and the rest of the suite pass

checklist.judge: Does this change restructure the code toward the plan's target while keeping behaviour identical? FAIL if it edits, weakens or skips a pinned test, changes a public signature or output the invariants cover, or adds behaviour the plan does not mention.

work_packages.title: Prove the invariants
work_packages.instructions:
Read the plan, the pinned tests and the refactored code, then write ${notes_dir}/refactor-review.md: one line
per invariant naming its id, whether it still holds and the test that shows it, then the steps from the plan
that were done, changed or dropped, and why.

checklist.assert: the review names every invariant id from the plan
checklist.cmd: ids=$(grep -oE '^INV[0-9]+' ${notes_dir}/refactor.md) || exit 1; for id in $ids; do grep -qw "$id" ${notes_dir}/refactor-review.md || { echo "$id is not reviewed"; exit 1; }; done

checklist.assert: the review carries at least 80 words

checklist.judge: Does this review check each invariant against a named test and account for every planned step? FAIL if it marks an invariant as holding without naming the test that shows it, skips a step from the plan, or claims something the code does not show.

work_packages.title: Refactor gate
work_packages.instructions: The refactor is done only when everything still passes
